findings.title: Web client still reads `invoice.amount`, which the API no longer returns
findings.explanation: The serializer now returns `amount_cents` and no longer returns `amount`. `InvoiceRow.tsx` still renders `money.format(invoice.amount / 100)`. `invoice.amount` is now `undefined`, so the invoice table will show `NaN`. The `Invoice` type in `web/src/api/invoices.ts` (line 4) still declares `amount: number // cents`, so TypeScript won't catch the mismatch. Update the type and the component to use `amount_cents` in this PR.

findings.title: Breaking API change with no compatibility period
findings.explanation: Removing `amount` from the `/invoices` list and detail responses breaks every existing consumer. These include external API clients, and the web frontend during a rolling deploy when old frontend code meets the new backend. Return both `amount` and `amount_cents` for a deprecation window, then remove `amount` later. Alternatively, version the API and announce the change. Deploy the frontend change so that it tolerates both fields before the backend stops sending `amount`.

findings.title: Check for other consumers and docs that reference the old field name
findings.explanation: I found no other in-repo users of the serialized `amount`. Still, check the OpenAPI spec, docs, SDKs, tests and webhook payloads for the old name. Consider adding or updating a serializer test that asserts the `amount_cents` shape.
